note: ORC/MCM ChIP-exo in G1 and G2 arrest (Reuter et al. 2024), the G1/G2 arm of GSE240779 (subseries GSE173527). Served as deposited: the combined tracks are the submitters' own CPM bigWigs copied byte-for-byte, the strand-split tracks are their raw read coverage multiplied by one per-sample factor of 1e6/mapped reads, since the deposit leaves them un-normalised and the six libraries differ 1.45-fold in depth. Containers are the comparisons the paper makes: ORC against MCM in G1, ORC in G1 against G2, and each condition's two biological replicates against each other; the strand containers carry the plus/minus asymmetry that puts the edges of an ORC or MCM footprint on screen. Scale is the hard part of this dataset and the viewLimits here are set from origins, not from extremes. ChIP-exo peak height spans two and a half orders of magnitude: genome-wide maxima are 11,066-12,581 on the Orc2 tracks and 65,917-93,760 on the Mcm4 tracks, but those are a handful of loci, and a scale that fits them renders a real origin as a flat line. Measured instead over the 839 OriDB v3 origin intervals this hub already carries, the tallest point inside an origin has a median of 38-98 and a 90th percentile of 300-546 across the combined tracks, and 16-25 and 78-141 across the strand tracks. The caps of 0:600 and -150:150 therefore hold nine origins in ten on scale; the strongest decile clips, so the validator's clipping warning for every track in this dataset is expected, and a reader measuring absolute peak height should switch the track to autoScale. Combined and strand tracks get different caps on purpose: both are per million reads, but the combined track extends reads to ~209 bp and so sits about 4.2x higher.
